page.layout: One printed page. Top: a verse stanza in italic, followed by a signature line. Below a rule: a dedication heading in letterspaced capitals, then a line in italic and a short line of text. The lower text is faint and largely show-through from the reverse side, so it is only partly legible.

p.i: Probant, atque maligni, Mores his rebus digni, Sanus esse non potes, Ni multum vinum potes, Caula sordibus scatet, Aula fraudibus patet, Fallit sæpe Electio, In spe fit deceptio, Quare vt quidlibet sies, Vir bonus nunquam fies.

page.notes: The lower body of the second section is very faint; most of its lines are show-through from the reverse side and could not be read, so they are marked illegible. The heading "VENERABILI DOMINO," and the dedication lines are read with doubt, and the letterspaced heading may be partly mirrored show-through. Verse lines are run together within one paragraph per stanza. No running head, page number, catchword or signature is visible. The large initial Q of "Quare" is a swash letter.
